verdicts.reason: A: the three plan cards are drawn at very different sizes. Family is huge and the Yearly and Monthly cards are tiny, so their labels can't be read and the original hierarchy, where the dark Yearly card was the hero, is flipped. The cards are scattered left and right around a ragged, left-aligned subtitle. B: the cards are a consistent size but far too small, so their labels can't be read. They are out of order (Yearly and Family on top, Monthly stranded alone below the subtitle), and the subtitle sits between the cards; the logo has also moved to the right edge. B wins narrowly, only because its cards are at least the same scale.
